summary: 自由游戏让孩子练习协商、表达意图和尝试不同角色。儿童和动物研究还提示，游戏可能帮助缓解焦虑、发展社交能力及想象力，成人过度安排活动则会压缩这些机会。

paragraphs.brief: 虽然人们早已认识到游戏的好处一直持续到成年，但美国心理学家现在却担心没有游戏实际上会伤害他们国家的孩子们。
sentences: While it has long been recognized that play affords benefits that last through adulthood, psychologists in the US are now becoming concerned that lack of play could actually be harming their country’s kids.
虽然人们早已认识到游戏的好处一直持续到成年，但美国心理学家现在却担心没有游戏实际上会伤害他们国家的孩子们。
In the past, few children grew up without ample free-play time.
过去，很少有儿童长大后没有充足的自由游戏时间。
But youngsters’ leisure hours are now filled with structured activities such as music lessons and sports.
但青少年的闲暇时间现在充斥着诸如音乐课和体育等有组织的活动。
Kids play soccer, Scrabble and saxophone – so why are experts worried that these activities are eating into free play?
孩子们玩足球、拼字游戏和萨克斯风，为什么专家担心这些活动是免费的？
Most games are fun and sources of learning experiences – fostering group cohesion, for instance, says educational psychologist Anthony Pellegrini.
比如说教育心理学家安东尼·佩列格里尼：“多数游戏是有趣的，是学习经验的源泉 -- -- 培养群体凝聚力。”
But, Pellegrini explains, “games have predetermined rules – set up in advance and followed.
但Pellegrini解释道，“游戏已经预先确定了规则，事先制定并遵循了。
Play, on the other hand, does not have rules, so affords more creative responses.
另一方面，游戏没有规则，因此可以提供更有创造性的反应。
Children initiate and create free play, and use their imagination to try out new activities and roles.”
儿童发起并创造自由游戏，利用他们的想象力尝试新的活动和角色。”

paragraphs.brief: 也许最重要的是，玩耍有助于我们发展强大的社会技能。
sentences: Perhaps most crucially, play helps us develop strong social skills.
也许最重要的是，玩耍有助于我们发展强大的社会技能。
“You don’t become socially competent via teachers telling you how to behave,” Pellegrini says.
佩列格里尼说：“老师教你怎么表现，你就不会有社交能力。”
“Kids learn those skills by interacting with peers, learning what is and isn’t acceptable.
“孩子们通过与同龄人互动学习这些技能，学习什么是和什么是不可接受。
They want this thing to keep going, so they’re willing to ‘go the extra mile’ to accommodate their playmates’ desires.
他们希望这件事能继续下去，所以他们愿意“多走几英里”，以适应玩伴的欲望。
Keeping things friendly requires communication – arguably the most valuable social skill of all.
保持友好需要沟通 — — 可以说是所有人最宝贵的社会技能。
Play among peers is the most important in this regard.”
在这方面，同龄人之间的游戏是最重要的。”
Studies show that children use more sophisticated language when playing with other children than when playing with adults.
研究表明，儿童在与其他儿童玩耍时比在与成人玩耍时使用更复杂的语言。

In pretend play, for instance, they have to communicate about something that’s not physically present, so they have to use complicated language to communicate what it is that they’re trying to say,” Pellegrini explains.
佩列格里尼解释：“例如，在假装玩耍时，他们必须交流一些身体上不存在的东西，所以他们不得不使用复杂的语言来交流他们想要表达的。”

paragraphs.brief: 如果玩耍有助于儿童融入社会，那么玩耍的缺乏就会阻碍社会发展 — — 研究表明它确实如此。
sentences: If play helps children become socialized, then lack of play should impede social development – and research suggests that it does.
如果玩耍有助于儿童融入社会，那么玩耍的缺乏就会阻碍社会发展 — — 研究表明它确实如此。

A study of children in Michigan revealed that kids who enrolled in play-oriented preschools were more socially adjusted later in life – and less likely to commit a felony or be suspended from work – than kids who attended play-free preschools where they were constantly instructed by teachers.
对密歇根州儿童进行的一项研究表明，在以玩耍为导向的学前班注册的儿童，比在教师经常教导的无玩耍学前班上学的儿童，在晚年社会上更能适应社会因素 — — 更不可能犯重罪或被停职。

paragraphs.brief: 2003年的一项研究甚至指出，游戏可以促进动物的情感和社会发展。
sentences: A 2003 study even suggests that play promotes emotional and social development in animals.
2003年的一项研究甚至指出，游戏可以促进动物的情感和社会发展。
Researchers allowed thirteen rats to play freely with companions for three and a half days, and kept fourteen others isolated for the same period.
研究人员允许13只大鼠与同伴自由玩耍三天半，而同期则将另外14只老鼠隔离。
Examination revealed that the brains of the rats which had played contained much higher levels of BDNF – a protein that stimulates the growth of new neurons – than those of the animals that had not.
检查发现，玩耍的老鼠的大脑含有比没有的动物的大脑高得多的BDNF — — 一种刺激新神经元生长的蛋白质。
“I think play is the major mechanism whereby higher regions of the brain get socialized,” says neuroscientist Jaak Panksepp, who co-authored the study.
说神经科学家Jaak Panksepp 共同撰写了这份研究：“我认为玩耍是大脑高端被社会化的主要机制。”

paragraphs.brief: 与聆听故事的焦虑儿童相比，焦虑儿童的焦虑程度下降了两倍多。
sentences: Research also suggests that imaginative play is critical for children’s emotional health, as it enables them to work through anxiety.
研究还表明，富有想象力的游戏对于儿童的情感健康至关重要，因为这使他们得以通过焦虑而工作。
In a 1984 study, researchers assessed the anxiety levels of seventy-four children on their first day of preschool.
在1984年的一项研究中，研究人员评估了74名儿童在学龄前第一天的焦虑程度。
They labeled each child as either “anxious” or “not anxious”, then randomly split the kids into groups.
他们把每个孩子都说成是 " 焦虑 " 或 " 不焦虑 "，然后随意地把孩子分成几个群体。
Half were escorted to rooms full of toys, where they played for 15 minutes; the other half listened to a teacher tell a story for 15 minutes.
一半人被押送到装满玩具的房间，在那里玩了15分钟；另一半人听老师讲一个故事15分钟。
Afterward, their levels were assessed again.
其后，又对它们的水平进行了评估。
The anxiety levels of the anxious kids who had played had dropped by more than twice as much compared with the anxious kids who had listened to the story.
与聆听故事的焦虑儿童相比，焦虑儿童的焦虑程度下降了两倍多。

paragraphs.brief: 研究者们接着介绍了另一个老鼠，一个从未接触过领子、也不害怕的老鼠，它开始与其中一只老鼠玩耍。
sentences: Results of animal studies support these views.
动物研究的结果支持了这些观点。
In 2008, neuroscientist Stephen Siviy put rats into a chamber and exposed them to a collar previously worn by a cat, making them visibly anxious.
2008年，神经科学家Stephen Siviy将老鼠放入一个房间，暴露在以前被猫戴的项圈上，使他们明显焦虑不安。
Later, the chamber was cleaned to remove the cat odor, and the rats were put back without the collar.
后来，清理了房间以去除猫的气味，老鼠被放回没有领。
They immediately became anxious again, probably because they associated the space with the cat.
他们立刻又变得焦虑了可能是因为他们把空间和猫联系起来了
The researchers then introduced another rat – one that had never been exposed to the collar and was not afraid – and it began playing with one of the rats.
研究者们接着介绍了另一个老鼠，一个从未接触过领子、也不害怕的老鼠，它开始与其中一只老鼠玩耍。
“Shortly thereafter, the first rat relaxed and became calm,” says Siviy, “suggesting that play helped lessen its anxiety.”
”Siviy说，“不久之后，第一只老鼠放松了，变得平静了，“建议玩这个游戏有助于减轻它的焦虑。

paragraphs.brief: 在一项经典研究中，研究人员告诉一群学龄前儿童，可以自由地玩弄一些共同的东西，如纸巾、螺丝刀、木板和纸夹。
sentences: Play even appears to make kids smarter.
玩耍甚至让孩子们更聪明
In a classic study, researchers told a group of preschool children to play freely with some common objects such as paper towels, a screwdriver, a wooden board and paper clips.
在一项经典研究中，研究人员告诉一群学龄前儿童，可以自由地玩弄一些共同的东西，如纸巾、螺丝刀、木板和纸夹。
Another group was asked to imitate an experimenter using the objects in common ways.
另一个小组被要求以共同的方式模仿实验者使用这些物体。
A third set was told to sit and draw whatever they wanted, without seeing the objects.
第三组被叫坐下来画他们想要的东西却没看到那些东西
After 10 minutes, the researchers asked the children to come up with ideas for how one of the objects could be used.
10分钟后，研究人员要求孩子们提出如何使用其中一种物体的想法。

The kids who had played with the objects named, on average, three times as many nonstandard, creative uses for the objects as those in either of the other two groups did, suggesting that play fosters imaginative thinking.
玩过这些被命名为非标准、创造性的物品的孩子们平均是其他两个团体的三倍这表明游戏能促进想象力思维

paragraphs.brief: 在没有游戏的情况下，儿童错过了重要的学习经验。”
sentences: A later animal study produced similar results.
后来的一项动物研究得出了类似的结果。
Experimenters isolated young rats during the development period when they would have most frequently played.
实验者在发育期孤立了幼鼠，当时它们最经常玩耍。
The researchers taught these rats, and a group that had been allowed to play without constraints, to pull a rubber ball out of the way to get a food treat.
研究人员教这些大鼠和一群被允许不受限制地玩耍的老鼠，把橡皮球从路上拉出来，以获得食物。
A few days later they switched the setup so the rats would have to push the same ball to get the treat.
几天后他们换了套子老鼠们不得不推同一个球才能得到治疗
Compared with the isolated rats, the ones which had played proved to be far more adept at solving problems.
与孤立的老鼠相比，那些玩耍的老鼠更擅长解决问题。
“Play is like a kaleidoscope,” says evolutionary biologist Marc Bekoff, “in that it is random and creative.
进化生物学家Marc Bekoff说，“游戏就像一个千字眼，” 因为它是随机的和创造性的。
It encourages flexibility and creativity that may, in the future, be advantageous in unexpected situations or new environments.
它鼓励灵活性和创造性，将来在意想不到的情况或新的环境中可能是有益的。
And in the absence of play, children miss vital learning experiences.”
在没有游戏的情况下，儿童错过了重要的学习经验。”

items.en: reference to how play can develop children’s verbal skills
items.zh: 有关游戏如何培养儿童语言技能的参考
items.why: 在假装游戏中要谈论并不在场的事物，孩子不得不用更复杂的语言把意思说清楚。

items.en: mention of a change in the amount of free play children engage in
items.zh: 提到儿童自由玩耍的数量变化
items.why: 题目问“提到自由玩于时间的变化”。A段对比“过去有很多自由玩下时间”vs“现在被课程和活动占满”,非常清楚地说明了自由游戏在减少。其他段不是在讲时间趋势。

items.en: an account of some research indicating that free play stimulates children’s creativity
items.zh: 一些研究的叙述表明自由游戏刺激儿童的创造力
items.why: 玩过物品的孩子能想出约三倍之多的非寻常用途，给出了自由游戏激发创造力的实验结果。

items.en: evidence of the link between antisocial behaviour and a lack of free play
items.zh: 反社会行为与缺乏自由游戏之间联系的证据
items.why: 题目里的“antisocial behaviour” 可以体现在“犯罪 (commit a felony)”“被停职(suspended from work)”这种反社会、违反规范的表现。C 段明确说: 缺少玩页的孩子，长大后更容易出现这种问题 = 有联系。

items.en: a comparison between free play and other forms of play
items.zh: 自由游戏与其他形式游戏的比较
items.why: 题目问“比较自由游戏和其他形式的游戏"。A段区分了: 有规则的 (soccer Scrabble, etc.) vs 自由的 (play),并强调规则性 vs 开放性。这正是对比。

items.en: It encourages children to take other people’s wishes into account.
items.zh: 它鼓励儿童考虑他人的愿望。

items.en: It can serve to relieve stress.
It prepares children for dealing with unpredictable situations.
items.zh: 它使儿童为应付无法预测的情况做好准备。

items.en: It is less useful for children when adults are involved.
items.zh: 当成年人参与时，它对儿童用处不大。

items.en: In studies researching links between play and social learning, experiments analysing protein levels in the ________ of rats noted significant differences between rats which had played and those which had not.
items.zh: 研究游戏与社会性学习的实验分析了大鼠________中的蛋白质水平，发现玩过的大鼠和没有玩过的大鼠之间存在显著差异。
items.why: 回到对应内容“检查发现，玩耍的老鼠的大脑含有比没有的动物的大脑高得多的BDNF — — 一种刺激新神经元生长的蛋白质”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: In another study, rats made distressed by an object smelling of a ________ experienced a noticeable reduction in their ____ (Q25) levels after they had been allowed to play.
items.zh: 另一项研究用带有________气味的物体使大鼠不安。允许它们玩耍后，它们的________（Q25）水平明显下降。
items.why: 回到对应内容“2008年，神经科学家Stephen Siviy将老鼠放入一个房间，暴露在以前被猫戴的项圈上，使他们明显焦虑不安”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: In another study, rats made distressed by an object smelling of a ____ (Q24) experienced a noticeable reduction in their ________ levels after they had been allowed to play.
items.zh: 另一项研究用带有________（Q24）气味的物体使大鼠不安。允许它们玩耍后，它们的________水平明显下降。
items.why: 回到对应内容“”Siviy说，“不久之后，第一只老鼠放松了，变得平静了，“建议玩这个游戏有助于减轻它的焦虑”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: A further experiment, in which rats had to move a ________ in order to reach a reward, indicated that rats deprived of play were less skilled at dealing with problems.
items.zh: 还有一项实验要求大鼠移动一个________才能取得奖励。结果表明，缺少玩耍机会的大鼠较不善于解决问题。
items.why: 空格问的是movea _ inorderto reach a reward. H段明确是“a rubber ball”。在一词限制下，填 ball。它体现的是解决问题的灵活性和适应性。被隔离、没玩豆的老鼠表现更差，说明游戏训练了解决新情况的能力。

points: 题目问“比较自由游戏和其他形式的游戏"。A段区分了: 有规则的 (soccer Scrabble, etc.) vs 自由的 (play),并强调规则性 vs 开放性。这正是对比。

clauses: …, psychologists in the US are now becoming concerned that lack of play could actually be harming their country’s kids.
连接词 while 引出“While it has long been recognized that play affords benefits that last through adulthood”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
Kids play soccer, Scrabble and saxophone – so why are experts worried …?
“that these activities are eating into free play”补足 worried 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 worried 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: Free play makes us better adjusted, smarter and less stressed
自由游戏能让我们更适应更聪明压力更小
